traits.build_notes: Middle blockers are the tallest and heaviest players on the team with an ectomorphic build: long legs and very long arms, narrow relative to height, lean (systematic review of the MB; Croatian 13-15 y study: MBs taller and more ectomorphic). Stature: London 2012 Olympic men's MBs 203.8 +/- 4.9 cm (Tsukuba study); top men's MB profiles 2.05-2.09 m (Holt, Piano); women's elite MBs 1.88-1.98 m (Erdem 188, Akinradewo 191, Danesi 195-198); 2017 FIVB U18 girls' MBs 185.9 cm / 71.4 kg; 13-15 y club girls' MBs 174.9 +/- 8.5 cm. U16 value 1.80 m is an estimate between those two youth data sets. Reach: men's MB spike/block 345.6/321.3 cm (Palao et al. 2014 as cited by the MB systematic review, Olympics/World Championships 2000-2012; not checked against the original table); top men's MB profiles 349-357 / 320-338 cm; women: profiles spike 308-315 (Akinradewo 330) / block 300-306 cm, U18 girls' MBs 294.5 / 282.7 cm; women's elite and U16 values are estimates between these, and roster reach values are self-reported and often generous. traits.build_notes: ALL NUMBERS ESTIMATED: no anthropometric source could be opened in this session because page fetches were blocked and the shared web-search budget ran out. The values are typical figures for international outside hitters (Volleyball World/VNL rosters list height, spike and block reach per player; roster reach values are self-reported and tend to run high) and should be checked before use. Standing reach is taken as ~1.29-1.30 x stature. Spike reach is standing reach + ~0.90 m (men), ~0.65 m (women) or ~0.47 m (U16 girls); block reach is ~0.20 m (men) or ~0.10 m (women and girls) below spike reach. Body build: outside hitters are the all-round passer-attackers, tall but usually a few cm shorter than middle blockers and opposites, with a long-limbed, lean athletic build, strong legs and hips, and a well-developed hitting shoulder and back. Studies support a few qualitative points: upper-body anthropometrics and joint angular velocities matter most for ball speed (Fuchs et al. 2019), men jump higher and use more torso and arm swing than women (Fuchs et al. 2019), and OH/OPP plant with a much deeper knee than middle blockers (Frontiers in Physiology 2026). Gear (visual convention, estimated): knee pads on both knees, usually low-profile sleeve pads worn just below the knee, plus ankle braces or high-top volleyball shoes. Some players wear compression arm sleeves and finger or wrist tape. Women wear fitted shorts and men longer shorts. The outside hitter wears the normal team jersey; only the libero wears a contrasting shirt.

techniques.description: Many elite setters jump-float: after a short (2-3 step) approach and a low toss, ball is struck with a firm wrist just after the peak of a modest jump (~0.3 m), arm high in front of the hitting shoulder, trunk nearly square, legs slightly flexed with plantarflexed ankles.

traits.build_notes: ALL TRAIT NUMBERS ARE ESTIMATES (position-specific means could not be read from full texts). Basis: elite men setters profiled 1.98-2.00 m with spike 345-363 cm and block 320-340 cm (Giannelli, Christenson - tall examples); professional men overall spike ~3.43 m / block ~3.27 m (cited from Palao 2014) and setters are generally shorter than hitters/middles, so typical elite setter set slightly lower. Elite women setters profiled 1.78-1.88 m, spike 303-313 cm, block 279-305 cm (Orro, Wolosz, Poulter); elite women overall ~1.82 m with ~2.34 m reach (Valades & Palao). Standing reach estimated as ~1.29-1.30 x stature. U16 girls: competitive (regional/national-pathway) setters estimated ~1.71 m; Serbian U17 national-team mean ~1.77 m (all positions) and setters are shorter than hitters/middles in youth samples; club-level U16 setters will often be 1.62-1.70 m. Build: lean, athletic, usually lighter and shorter than middles/opposites, with lower squat strength and jump than hitters (Marques 2009; national-team data); long arms and strong fingers/wrists matter more than mass. Gear: regular team jersey (not the contrasting libero shirt), shorts (women: spandex), low-profile knee pads, court shoes; ankle braces and finger tape (buddy-taped fingers) are common on setters. Right-handed setter assumed; left-handed setters are mirrored.
